sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
A role process that hangs (alive, no output, no exit) waits for the owner to notice and stop it. ork finds a lost process only when the daemon starts (`internal/engine/recover.go:49-114`), and no code in `internal/agent` or `internal/engine` kills a role that is alive but silent. The guide tells the owner to open a stale-looking run, read the last output and stop it by hand (S165 `docs/guide.md`, section 12).

Parity row: 7.4 (stale runs; the watchdog half) and gap 18 of the prioritized list in `docs/orchestrator-parity.md` (from S165).

What the code shows:
- The adapters already kill the whole process group when the context they are given ends (`internal/agent/claude/run.go:25,55-61`, `internal/agent/codex/codex.go:203-223`, `internal/clirun/procgroup_unix.go:14-31`). A watchdog only has to end that context.
- Every vendor stream event reaches the engine as `Request.OnEvent`, and assistant text as `OnLive` (`internal/engine/runner.go:57-61`, `internal/daemon/runner.go:41-66,113-122`); `startActivity` counts them (`internal/engine/activity.go:41-62`). No time of the last event is kept.
- ork's own heartbeat posts `relay-run step ... --phase start` every 10 minutes while a role runs (`internal/engine/round.go:555-582`). The Running row's `!` and `!!` cues are read from the ledger's `updated_at` (`internal/tui/relayboard.go:132-150`). *Not verified*: whether that heartbeat keeps a hung role's ledger run fresh, so that the cue never shows. If it does, the cue cannot warn about a hung role, and the watchdog must read the engine's own event time.

Owner decisions that apply: none decide a hung role. adj 101 engine.pause-resume lets the owner retry a paused role; `lost` is a retryable pause kind already (`internal/runrec/record.go:143`, `docs/design.md` Owner questions and `retry`). ork never kills anything it did not start (`internal/engine/recover.go:56-71`); the watchdog kills only the process group it recorded for the role (`OnStart`, `internal/engine/round.go:290`).

Slicer check (`slicer find "watchdog"`, `"hung"`, `--root ../slicer`): no match. Slicer's ledger marks a run `stale` itself; it does not run or kill ork's role processes, and ork must not leave that to a ledger flag.

Design (*proposed*):
- A watchdog on every role round of a run. It records the time of the last event or live text from the role and, when the role has been silent for longer than a limit, ends the role's own context. The default limit is 30 minutes, the stale cutoff the Running row already uses (`docs/dashboard.md:495-498`). A negative `Deps.HungAfter` turns it off; zero means the default.
- A killed role is recorded as exit `hung`, its ledger step ends `fail`, the heartbeat stops, and the run pauses as `lost` with a reason that names the role, the round, the limit and the killed process group. It does not fall back to the next row and does not mark a vendor out (S169): a hang is not a limit. The owner retries with `t` or `ork retry RUN`; the retry runs the same row, with the "Earlier process lost" brief section the engine already writes (`internal/engine/round.go:137-138`).
- An owner stop during the role stays a stop (`cancelled`), not a hang.

Not in this slice: a project or registry setting for the limit (see Open), the spec-check role (its own loop, `internal/engine/speccheck.go:193-231`), the checks command (it has its own timeout, `check_minutes`), ending a ledger run that ork did not start (gap 10), automatic retry.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestSilentRoleIsKilledAfterTheLimitAndTheRunPausesAsLost` (`internal/engine/watchdog_test.go`): a fake runner that emits nothing and blocks until its context ends, with `HungAfter` 50ms: the runner's context ends, the role record has exit `hung` and an end time, and the run is `paused` with pending kind `lost`, the role, the round and a reason that names the limit and the killed process group.
- `TestEventsKeepARoleAlive`: a runner that calls `OnEvent` every 20ms for 300ms with `HungAfter` 100ms finishes `ok` and is never cancelled.
- `TestLiveTextCountsAsAnEvent`: the same with `OnLive` only.
- `TestHungRoleDoesNotFallBackOrMarkAVendorOut`: with a two-row chain, the second row never runs and no vendor is marked out.
- `TestRetryAfterAHungRoleRunsTheSameRowWithTheLostBrief`: `Retry` runs the same row again; its brief has the "Earlier process lost" section with the hung reason; `currentEntry` has not advanced.
- `TestHungRoleEndsItsLedgerStepAsFailAndStopsTheHeartbeat` (uses the harness of `internal/engine/heartbeat_test.go`): one `fail` step call, no `start` call after the kill.
- `TestOwnerStopDuringARoleIsCancelledNotHung`: `Stop` gives role exit `cancelled` and a `stopped` run, no pause.
- `TestNegativeHungAfterTurnsTheWatchdogOff` and `TestZeroHungAfterMeansThirtyMinutes`: a silent role is left alone with `HungAfter` -1; the default constant is 30 minutes.
- `TestTwoHungSiblingRoundsPauseOnce`: the reviewer and the UI pass of one state both silent: one pause, both role records `hung`.
- `TestDaemonRunsUseTheThirtyMinuteWatchdog` (`internal/daemon/runs_test.go`): `runDeps` carries the default and a `cfg.Engine` value is kept.
- `TestPausedHungRunShowsTheReasonAndRetry` (`internal/tui/runcard_test.go`): a paused run with pending `lost` and the hung reason shows the reason and the `t retry` hint in the pane; golden `engine-paused-hung-100x30.txt`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
UI slice: UI pass (r14) (docs/dashboard.md and a golden). Test-first: write the tests above, see them fail, then:
1. `internal/engine/engine.go:45-60`: add `Deps.HungAfter time.Duration` (0 means `defaultHungAfter = 30 * time.Minute`, negative turns the watchdog off), next to `HeartbeatEvery` (`:57`). Tests set it to milliseconds.
2. `internal/engine/watchdog.go` (new): `type roleWatch` with `touch()` (stores the time under a mutex or atomic), `start(ctx, kill func()) (stop func(), hung func() (silent time.Duration, was bool))`. A goroutine like the heartbeat (`round.go:555-582`) checks at `min(limit/4, 30s)` and, when `now - last > limit` and the role is still running, sets the flag once and calls `kill`. Use `e.d.now()` for the clock, as `overBudget` does.
3. `internal/engine/round.go:284-291`: make `runCtx, kill := context.WithCancel(ctx)`; wrap `OnEvent` and `OnLive` so each calls `watch.touch()` before the existing activity hook (`startActivity` and `liveHook`, `:284,289`); pass `runCtx` to `e.d.Runner.Run`. The watch starts just before `Runner.Run`, after any vendor-slot wait (S169), so a wait is never counted; it does not depend on `OnStart`, which a fake runner may not call.
4. `internal/engine/round.go:293-306`: the existing `ctx.Err()` check is on the parent `ctx`, so an owner stop still takes that path first. After it, if `watch` reports hung: update the role record (`EndedAt`, `Exit = "hung"`, `Session = res.Session`, tokens), `stop()` the heartbeat, `e.stepEnd(ctx, rec, stepID, "fail")`, then `return outcome{}, e.pause(runrec.Pending{Kind: runrec.PendingLost, State: r.state, Role: r.role, Round: r.n, Reason: ...})`. Reason: `ROLE round N hung: no output for LIMIT; its process group PGID was killed` (PGID is read from the role record that `OnStart` fills, `:290`; leave the clause out when it is 0). This sits before the `class` switch (`:307-314`), so the exit is never `ExitError` and never reaches the fallback test (`:329-330`).
5. `internal/engine/engine.go:171-203`: no change needed: a `hung` record matches its entry and is not a fallback exit, so `currentEntry` stays on the row (`TestRetryAfterAHungRoleRunsTheSameRowWithTheLostBrief` pins it). `pendingSection` (`round.go:137-138`) already turns `lost` into the retry brief.
6. `internal/daemon/runs.go:149-158`: nothing to wire if the default is in the engine; the daemon test pins that a `cfg.Engine` value is respected.
7. Docs: `docs/design.md:690-700` (the watchdog beside the heartbeat) and `:1028-1034` (retry covers a hung role), `docs/dashboard.md:495-505` (the cue cannot be relied on for a hung role, and the watchdog pauses at 30 minutes) and `:700-706`, `docs/state.md:388-396` (`lost` also means a hung role), `docs/guide.md` section 12 (S165): a silent role is killed and paused for you.
8. Goldens: `go test ./internal/tui -update`; review `testdata/golden/` (only `engine-paused-hung-100x30.txt` is new).
Order: independent of S166, S167, S168. S169 edits the same `runRound` (`round.go:262-292`) before the runner call; this slice edits the runner call and what follows. Land either first and rebase.
Not verified: that a Claude or Codex role emits an event at least every few minutes during a long silent tool call (a 12 minute `go test` inside a role). If it does not, 30 minutes could kill a healthy role. No real vendor run was made.
Open: the limit. Options: (a) a fixed 30 minutes in code, with `Deps.HungAfter` for tests (recommended: no registry change; matches the stale cutoff); (b) a project setting `hung_minutes` with `ork projects set --hung-minutes N`, which touches the registry file format and belongs with gap 7.2; (c) the limit follows `check_minutes` (the project's check timeout, default 10), which is shorter than the stale cutoff and risks killing a long silent tool call. Second: after a hang, the run pauses for the owner (recommended: nothing is retried blind). The option is one automatic retry on the same row, then a pause.
